Myeloma can give small, multiple "punched-out" lytic lesions, or expansile lesions that swell the bone leaving a thin cortical shell (appearance similar to plasmacytoma). In T10 the body is replaced by low-density tissue: with the cortex so thin the risk of collapse is high, and if the tissue breaches the posterior wall it can compress the cord. For this reason, besides counting the lesions, the report must state: integrity of the posterior wall, extension into the canal or paravertebral tissues, stability (SINS score), and suggest MRI if there are pain or neurologic signs.

With dual-energy CT the calcium-suppressed map shows the marrow content: dark (fat) where normal, bright where infiltrated.

Differential diagnosis of expansile lytic vertebral lesions: kidney and thyroid metastases, plasmacytoma, aggressive hemangioma, giant cell tumor, aneurysmal bone cyst (young patients).
Davanti a una lesione litica vertebrale,: Faced with a lytic vertebral lesion, always look at the posterior wall and the canal: they decide the urgency.
